items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your average blood sugar was 306.2 mg/dL, which is above 250, so contact your care team today. Only 0.0% of your readings were in the 70-180 range, which is something to discuss with your team.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: You walked after 3 of your scored meals, which is too few to see how it affects you. Walking after dinner is associated with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in blood sugar.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: About 26.7% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later, which is associated with sugar rising about 9.2 mg/dL more. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see how it affects your blood sugar.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 14.4 hours, with 92.3% of nights reaching 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed blood sugar levels, but more research is needed to understand its effects.
